proposed_rules.trigger: A full-width bar at the very top of the page, above the hero, containing top-level menu labels ('Solutions Business Need Work O...'), present on every sampled page.
proposed_rules.decision: Map to the global nav/header fragment, not page content; exclude from the page's block inventory.
proposed_rules.rationale: Identical content and position across every packet analyzed indicates shared site chrome, not authored page content.

proposed_rules.trigger: A bottom-most sibling zone with a fixed marketing tagline ('The best no-code platform for...') plus a thin separator row.
proposed_rules.decision: Map to the global footer fragment; exclude from page-specific block inventory.

proposed_rules.trigger: The related-articles/blog grid at the page bottom sometimes renders as a single [3xN] node whose first text run includes what is elsewhere a separate heading (e.g. 'Find Inspiration on the Knack Blog'), instead of a distinct heading child node.
proposed_rules.decision: Treat the truncated leading text as the section heading (default-content) regardless of whether the capture produced a separate node; still emit the grid as ONE related-articles block. Rejected alternative: assume the heading is genuinely absent and omit it.
proposed_rules.rationale: Sibling pages with an identical component show the heading as a distinct node, so its absence here is most likely a capture/DOM-collapsing artifact rather than a real content difference.
